pages.title: Missiles and Missile Launchers
pages.text: Missile Launchers are linked and fired like ordinary weapons, but consume missiles as ammunition. After a brief period of straight flight, each missile homes in on the currently locked hostile target; see $(l:vsie:control_seat/radar)Control Seat: Radar and IFF/$. A Missile Launcher will not fire if IFF is not configured or no hostile target exists.

pages.title: Vertical Launch System
pages.text: A Vertical Launch System is more than a Missile Launcher pointed in another direction: it can control many missiles and launch them in sequence.$(br2)Its linking process differs from ordinary weapons. The system consists of a VLS Core linked to the Control Seat and any number of VLS Cells linked to that core. It will not fire if IFF is not configured or no hostile target exists.

pages.title: VLS: Core
pages.text: Use these steps to configure a Vertical Launch System:$(br2)1. Link a VLS Core to the Control Seat.$(br2)2. As with an ordinary weapon, assign a fire channel and load enough missiles into the core.$(br2)3. Enter the launch interval at the bottom of the GUI.

pages.title: VLS: Cells
pages.text: 4. Clear your Linker—or use a new one—then Shift-right-click the VLS Core to record it. In the desired firing order, Shift-right-click each installed VLS Cell to record it in the core. There is no cell limit.$(br2)5. When the player fires from the Control Seat, every VLS Core on an active channel launches its stored missiles using the configured cell order and interval.$(br2)6. VLS-launched missiles turn slightly better than missiles fired from ordinary launchers.
